# Omarchy-inspired

delulu-smash runs as an Omarchy web app (`SUPER+SHIFT+J`), and its user lives in Omarchy all day. So the
app's navigation and many of its other parts should feel like Omarchy: the same habits work in both.

## Rule

When designing navigation, keys, menus or look, check how Omarchy does it first, and copy its pattern
unless there's a reason not to. Only when Omarchy has nothing comparable (eg editor panes, result tabs),
borrow from the tools it ships or the user already knows: Zed, VS Code, Jupyter.

## Conventions

| Omarchy | delulu-smash |
| --- | --- |
| `SUPER` + one letter for desktop actions | `Alt` + one letter for app actions (`SUPER` belongs to the desktop) |
| `SUPER+K`: searchable list of every keybinding | `Alt+K`: the same list for the app's shortcuts |
| menus are a search box over a list: type to filter, arrows, Enter, Esc | the same for any app list or picker (keybindings list, the forms' choice input) |
| Esc closes the menu on top | Esc closes the top layer only (a menu before the floating view under it) |
| keyboard first, mouse works too | every action has a key or a click, ideally both |
| one theme for the desktop | the app's colors come from the theme palette, never one-off colors |

## Same key, `SUPER` → `Alt`

A guideline for new shortcuts: when an app action matches an Omarchy one, consider Omarchy's key with
`SUPER` swapped for `Alt`, so the habit carries over (eg `SUPER+K` keybindings → `Alt+K`, `SUPER+F` →
`Alt+F` full screen). It's something to keep in mind, not a hard rule.

The shortcuts that exist today (`ui/shortcuts.py`) are signed off by the user and stay as
they are, including ones whose letter means something else in Omarchy.

## Applying it

- New shortcuts: check for a matching Omarchy action (`omarchy menu keybindings --print`) and suggest
  its letter with `Alt`; otherwise `Alt` + a free letter. A browser may already use some `Alt` keys.
  Define them once in `ui/shortcuts.py`, so they show up in the `Alt+K` list automatically.
- New lists or pickers: reuse the search-box-over-a-list pattern (`assets/keys.js`, `assets/choice.js`)
  rather than a new kind of menu.
- When a choice knowingly differs from Omarchy, say why in the README.

## Not done yet

- The palette is Everforest, written into `assets/app.css`; it doesn't follow a change of Omarchy theme.
- In Omarchy's keybindings menu, Enter runs the picked binding. In the `Alt+K` list it does for the
  page-wide `Alt` keys only (`commands.RUNNABLE`), not for keys that act on what is being typed.
